Oxytocin is used for the prophy- laxis and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage (p.2003). In the active management of the third stage of labour, the combination of oxytocin and ergometrine may be associated with a small re- duction in the risk of postpartum haemorrhage compared with oxytocin alone, but a higher incidence of nausea, vomiting, and hypertension. Retained placenta. Oxytocin injected into the vein of the um- bilical cord has been used to assist the removal of retained pla- centa. A meta-analysis1 of 12 studies found evidence that oxy- tocin reduced the incidence of manual removal of the retained placenta, although there was no apparent benefit in terms of other measures including blood loss, curettage, and infection.
